JuntosA Mexico-first concept for AirbnbIndependent concept · public data

Group trips to concerts, planned together and paid by each friend, their way.

AI plans the trip from the concert tickets, the group picks the stay in a quick vote, and each friend pays their own part by card, SPEI transfer or cash. Nobody fronts the whole stay.

The problemMexicans travel to events in groups, but an Airbnb booking takes one payment method. The friend with a credit card fronts the whole stay and chases the rest.
Why LATAMMost adults don't have a bank credit card, groups already split costs (the cooperacha), and plans get made in WhatsApp. Airbnb retired its earlier Group Payments feature.
The opportunityInstallments helped Airbnb grow in Mexico, but they only reach card holders. Juntos brings the rest of the group in, starting with events Airbnb already sponsors.
Builds on an existing partnership · Airbnb is an official sponsor of Corona Capital 2026 through its global collaboration with Live Nation, OCESA's majority owner.
~85%of Corona Capital 2026 nights were booked by groups of 2+
~1 in 2Mexicans new to Airbnb in 2024 traveled in a group
30%of Airbnb split-payment bookings brought in a new user (2018)
15.7%of Mexican adults have a bank credit card
Sources: Airbnb Newsroom (Nov 2026; Jun 2025; split payments launch, 2018) · INEGI/CNBV ENIF 2024 · Airbnb Help Center. Not affiliated with Airbnb.
JuntosMexico-first concept for Airbnb

    Independent hypothesis by Daniel Fernandez, built from public information only. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Airbnb or WhatsApp, and not based on knowledge of Airbnb's roadmap. Shown in English for readability; the product would launch in Spanish. Listings, prices, the event and the payment methods shown are hypothetical. Photos: Unsplash.
